title: The Road Not Taken
sub: Four evenings, one stanza each. Every evening after the first adds the new stanza onto everything already learnt, so by Wednesday you are saying the whole thing.
source: Robert Frost, from Mountain Interval, 1916. Out of copyright.

poem.t: Two roads diverged in a yellow wood,
And sorry I could not travel both
And be one traveler, long I stood
And looked down one as far as I could
To where it bent in the undergrowth;
Then took the other, as just as fair,
And having perhaps the better claim,
Because it was grassy and wanted wear;
Though as for that the passing there
Had worn them really about the same,
And both that morning equally lay
In leaves no step had trodden black.
Oh, I kept the first for another day!
Yet knowing how way leads on to way,
I doubted if I should ever come back.
I shall be telling this with a sigh
Somewhere ages and ages hence:
Two roads diverged in a wood, and I—
I took the one less traveled by,
And that has made all the difference.

days.name: Sunday evening
days.blurb: The first stanza on its own. Two roads, and a man standing a long time at the place they part.

groups.label: Stanza 1
groups.note: Two roads diverged in a yellow wood

days.name: Monday evening
days.blurb: Stanza 2 on its own first, then stanzas 1 and 2 run together. The join is the part that trips people up, so it gets practised on the night it appears.

groups.label: Stanza 2
groups.note: Then took the other, as just as fair

days.name: Tuesday evening
days.blurb: Stanza 3 on its own, then the first three run together. Fifteen lines is most of the poem, and it is the first evening it starts to feel long.

groups.label: Stanza 3
groups.note: And both that morning equally lay

days.name: Wednesday evening
days.blurb: The last stanza, and then the whole poem end to end — the last one is the run that matters, because it is the one you do on Thursday.

groups.label: Stanza 4
groups.note: I shall be telling this with a sigh

groups.label: The whole poem
groups.note: All twenty lines — this is Thursday

last.name: Last words
last.tag: One blank at the end of each line
last.blurb: The lines are in front of you and only the last word of each is missing. The picture for the line you are on sits underneath from the start, so the two begin to go together.

first.name: First words
first.tag: One blank at the start of each line
first.blurb: Now the first word of each line is gone. Starting a line is the bit people get stuck on when they stand up to recite — and the picture is still there beside you.

half.name: Half gone
half.blurb: About half the words are away now, spread through. The shape of it is still there to lean on, and so is the picture.

line.name: Line by line
line.blurb: One whole line at a time, with the rest still around it. Look at the picture first and see whether the line comes.

heart.name: By heart
heart.blurb: No words on the screen at all — just the pictures you have had beside you the whole way up, one for each line, and you say it from memory.
